subject: Nehemiah
note: Evidence for Nehemiah's enhanced Bible figure page. Every quotation is in nehemiah.quotes.json and passes verify-quotes.mjs. Fetched texts are in design/saints-hub/sources/people/nehemiah/ (gitignored); the Fathers are the shared NPNF files. The page's Bible lines are the Berean Standard Bible (public domain); bsb-nehemiah.txt is the whole book copied from the shared BSB with each chapter's verses joined, so that lines running over a verse break can be checked. Sirach and 2 Maccabees are the World English Bible (shared/web-world-english-bible.txt).

life.text: Words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah; in Chislev of the twentieth year he was in the citadel of Susa; his brother Hanani came with men from Judah; the wall broken down and the gates burned; he sat, wept, mourned for days, fasting and praying.

His prayer: God of heaven who keeps His covenant; he confesses Israel's sins, 'Both I and my father's house have sinned'; reminds God of His word to Moses (scatter, then gather); ends asking success and mercy 'in the sight of this man'; he was cupbearer to the king.

Nisan of the twentieth year of Artaxerxes: he served the wine, had never been sad before the king; the king asked why; he was overwhelmed with fear; 'So I prayed to the God of heaven and answered the king'; the queen seated beside the king; he set a time; letters to the governors west of the Euphrates and to Asaph keeper of the king's forest for timber; granted 'because the gracious hand of my God was upon me'. Chislev (9th month) to Nisan (1st month) is four months; the page says 'Four months later'. The number tile for it was cut for space.

Army officers and cavalry sent with him; Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official disturbed; three days in Jerusalem; out at night with a few men, telling no one; one animal; Valley Gate, Well of the Serpent, Dung Gate, Fountain Gate, King's Pool, no room for the animal; up the valley by night; the officials did not know.
'Come, let us rebuild the wall'; 'Let us start rebuilding'; Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem mock: 'Are you rebelling against the king?'; 'The God of heaven is the One who will grant us success'.

The builders' list: Eliashib the high priest and the priests at the Sheep Gate (3:1); the Tekoite nobles 'did not put their shoulders to the work' (3:5), yet the Tekoites repaired a second section (3:27); Uzziel of the goldsmiths and Hananiah of the perfumers (3:8); Shallum, ruler of the other half-district of Jerusalem, 'with the help of his daughters' (3:12); priests in front of their own houses (3:28). Ten gates named: Sheep, Fish, Jeshanah, Valley, Dung, Fountain, Water, Horse, East, Inspection (3:1, 3, 6, 13, 14, 15, 26, 28, 29, 31); the list ends back at the Sheep Gate (3:32).

Sanballat: 'What are these feeble Jews doing?'; Tobiah's fox; wall joined to half its height; plot to attack; prayer and a guard day and night; families stationed with swords, spears and bows; 'Do not be afraid of them'; half the servants worked, half held spears, shields, bows and armour; carriers worked with one hand and held a weapon with the other; each builder with his sword strapped at his side; the trumpeter beside Nehemiah; rally at the sound of the horn; no one changed out of his clothes.
life.source: Nehemiah 4:1-23 (BSB). Josephus's parallel: 'the mason had his sword on, as well as he that brought the materials for building' (Antiquities 11.5.8). No trowel in either.

life.text: The outcry: mortgaged fields in a famine, borrowing for the king's tax, daughters already enslaved; Nehemiah 'extremely angry'; 'You are exacting usury from your own brothers!'; a large assembly; 'What you are doing is not right'; restore fields, vineyards, olive groves and houses; the oath; he shook out the folds of his robe; 'Amen'.

Governor from Artaxerxes' twentieth to thirty-second year, 'twelve years total'; neither he nor his brothers ate the governor's food allowance; earlier governors had burdened the people, 'But I did not do this, because of my fear of God'; 150 Jews and officials at his table besides guests from the nations; each day one ox, six choice sheep and fowl; 'Remember me favorably, O my God, for all that I have done for this people.'

The wall rebuilt, doors not yet hung; Sanballat and Geshem invite him to the plain of Ono, 'But they were planning to harm me'; 'I am doing a great work and cannot come down'; four times the same; the fifth time an unsealed letter by Sanballat's servant (revolt, king, prophets); 'There is nothing to these rumors'; Shemaiah son of Delaiah and the temple; 'Should a man like me run away?'; hired by Tobiah and Sanballat; Noadiah the prophetess. Completed in fifty-two days, on the twenty-fifth of Elul; the nations afraid and disheartened.
Doors set; Hanani and Hananiah, commander of the fortress, 'a faithful man who feared God more than most', over Jerusalem; gates not opened 'until the sun is hot'.

The Water Gate: Ezra reads the Law from daybreak to noon from a high wooden platform; all stood when he opened the book; the Levites explained it; the people wept; 'Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites' said 'This day is holy'; 8:10 'Then Nehemiah told them' in the BSB, 'Then he said to them' in the WEB (the speaker is not named in many translations); the Feast of Booths, booths on rooftops; not celebrated like this since Joshua son of Nun.
First name on the sealed covenant: 'Nehemiah the governor, son of Hacaliah'.

The dedication: Levites and singers with cymbals, harps and lyres; two great thanksgiving choirs on the wall, one to the right (Ezra the scribe led it), the other to the left with Nehemiah; both stood in the house of God; 'the joy of Jerusalem was heard from afar'.

Second stay: he had returned to Artaxerxes in the thirty-second year and came back 'some time later'; Eliashib the priest, a relative of Tobiah, had given Tobiah a large storeroom; he threw out Tobiah's goods; Levites unpaid and gone to their fields; Sabbath trade, gates shut, traders warned; marriages with women of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab, children who could not speak the language of Judah; he rebuked them, cursed, beat some and pulled out their hair; a son of Jehoiada son of Eliashib the high priest was Sanballat's son-in-law, driven away; wood and firstfruits arranged; 'Remember me' in 13:14, 22, 31, and 'Remember them' against the defilers in 13:29 (and 'remember Tobiah and Sanballat' in 6:14).
The temple was completed 'in the sixth year of the reign of King Darius'.

2 Maccabees, in the letter of the Jews of Jerusalem to those in Egypt: 'remember the fire which was given when Nehemiah offered sacrifices, after he had built both the temple and the altar' (1:18); the hidden fire, the thick liquid, the blaze when the sun shone out (1:19-22); the prayer with Jonathan leading (1:23-30); the liquid poured on large stones, a flame (1:31-32); the king of Persia enclosed the place and made it sacred (1:33-35); 'Nephthar', 'Cleansing' (1:36); Nehemiah's records and his library (2:13).
Sirach 49:13 praises Nehemiah after Zerubbabel and Jeshua; Ezra is not named anywhere in Sirach (searched the WEB text of SIR for Ezra and Esdras: no hits).

Josephus: Nehemiah cupbearer to Xerxes, hears Hebrew spoken by travellers outside Susa; the wall 'two years and four months', finished in the twenty-eighth year of Xerxes; the mason had his sword on; asks 'to finish the building of the temple'; 'he came to a great age, and then died'; 'a man of a good and righteous disposition ... an eternal monument for himself'.
life.source: Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews, book 11, chapter 5, sections 6-8, tr. Whiston (josephus-antiquities-11.txt).

life.text: Sulpicius Severus retells the story: 'very much beloved by Artaxerxes'; 'But Nehemiah, having stationed guards ... carried out what he had begun'.
life.source: Sulpicius Severus, Sacred History, Book 2, chapter 11 (shared/npnf211.txt).

life.text: Jerome, Letter 53 to Paulinus, 'Written in 394 A.D.': 'Ezra and Nehemiah, that is the Lord's helper and His consoler, are united in a single book...'
Ambrose retells the hidden fire from 2 Maccabees, calls him 'the priest Nehemiah' and 'holy Nehemiah', and says the sacrifice typifies the Holy Spirit and Christian baptism.
life.source: Ambrose, On the Duties of the Clergy, Book 3, chapters 17 and 18 (ambrose-duties-book-3.txt; also shared/npnf210.txt).

names.text: Tirshatha, 'the title of a Persian deputy or governor'; KJV keeps 'Tirshatha'; BDB notes the reading 'His Excellency' (after Meyer).
The book is 'Also called the second Book of Esdras (Ezra)', reckoned one book with Ezra in the Talmud and the early Church.
names.source: Catholic Encyclopedia, 1911, 'Book of Nehemiah', A. Van Hoonacker (catholic-encyclopedia-nehemiah-book.txt).

names.text: The date: 'the twentieth year of the Persian King Artaxerxes (445/444 B.C.)'.
names.source: OCA, 'Prophet Nehemiah' (oca-prophet-nehemiah.txt). NPNF 2/7 note to Cyril (shared/npnf207.txt) gives 'b.c. 444'.

feasts.text: Orthodox: the OCA lists 'Prophet Nehemiah' among the saints of the Sunday of the Forefathers ('The Sunday that falls between December 11-17'); its 2006 life page is dated 17 December, the Sunday that year.
feasts.source: OCA day page for 13 December 2026 (oca-2026-12-13-forefathers.txt) and 'Prophet Nehemiah' (oca-prophet-nehemiah.txt).

feasts.text: Azbuka Very: 'Святой Неемия, вождь иудейский', day of memory '(переходящая) - Неделя святых праотец', movable, the Sunday of the Holy Forefathers.

Catholic: no entry for Nehemiah in the 1916 Roman Martyrology, the 1969 Calendarium Romanum or the USCCB 2026 calendar (searched the shared files for Nehemia/Neemia/Nehemias: no hits). The 2004 Roman Martyrology in GCatholic's English rendering: all 36 monthly pages searched for Nehemia/Neemia, no hits; 13 July holds 'Commemoration of Saint Esdras, priest and scribe'.
feasts.source: shared/martyrology-1916.txt, calendarium-romanum-1969-ocr.txt, usccb-2026cal.txt; gcatholic.org/saints/data/martyrology2004-{1..12}{a,b,c}.htm (July b saved as gcatholic-martyrology2004-july-b.txt).

feasts.text: The '13 July (Catholic)' of Wikipedia's infobox cites the Vollständiges Heiligen-Lexikon, which says the opposite: at 13 July Neemias (with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak) is found with the Bollandists 'unter den Uebergangenen, da sie keine Verehrung genießen' (among those passed over, since they receive no veneration), Acta Sanctorum July III, 471.
feasts.source: zeno-heiligenlexikon-neemias.txt (Gemeinfrei). Wikipedia 'Nehemiah' used only as the lead.

feasts.text: Protestant: no day in the Church of England, Episcopal (LFF 2022), LCMS or ELCA calendars (shared files searched). The ELCA's Evangelical Lutheran Worship (final draft 2006) sets Nehemiah 1:4-11a for the Day of Penitence, and Nehemiah 8:1-3, 5-6, 8-10 for the Third Sunday after Epiphany, year C.
Coptic: no entry found in the Wikipedia list of the Coptic calendar on disk.

pictures.text: Band and card: 'Nehemiah looks upon the ruins of Jerusalem. Nehemiah ii. 17', plate signed 'J. James Tissot. Copyright by de Brunoff, 1904', in The Old Testament: three hundred and ninety-six compositions illustrating the Old Testament, volume 2 (Paris, M. de Brunoff, 1904), Internet Archive oldtestamentthre0002unse, leaf n286 (scan 3232 x 4609). Published 1904: public domain in the US; Tissot died 1902. Commons descriptions of the same series say its later plates were painted after Tissot's sketches by Michel Simonidy; Commons's own scan of this plate is tagged CC BY-SA 4.0 by its uploader, so it was NOT used; the Internet Archive scan of the 1904 book was used instead. Band: crop x 450-1900, y 900-2700, light blur (radius 1) against the print screen, 1450 x 1800, JPEG q80, 321 KB. Face at about 55% across, 42% down; posM and posD 50% 35%. Card: crop x 897-1597, y 1317-2192 resized to 480 x 600, eyes about 36% down, face centred.
pictures.source: Internet Archive item metadata and page image; viewed downscaled.

pictures.text: Portrait (-2): 'neemia alla corte di artaserse', attributed to Davide Ghirlandaio, Bible of Federico da Montefeltro, BAV Urb. lat. 1, f. 201r. Commons: {{PD-Art|PD-old-100}}, 1682 x 1067, source Silvia Blasio (ed.), Marche e Toscana, terre di grandi maestri tra Quattro e Seicento, Pacini, 2007. Cropped to the king's table (x 1010-1662, y 300-960): 652 x 660, q88. The faces are small at column width: a taste call for the owner.

Gallery (-3, wide screens only): 'Nehemiah the cup bearer', engraving, 1873, from The story of the Bible from Genesis to Revelation (HathiTrust uiug.30112065792167); Commons {{PD-1923}}, 1089 x 1533, resized to 724 x 1019 greyscale, q80, 234 KB.

Rejected: 'Prophet nehemiah.jpg' (a modern English-lettered icon wrongly tagged as over 100 years old, 600 px); the Florence Baptistery mosaic photo (CC BY 4.0); Sailko's photos of Gherardi's Cortona frescoes (CC BY-SA 4.0); Phillip Medhurst's Tissot scans (CC BY-SA 4.0); the Alcobaça, BnF, Cleveland and MET initials (faces too small); 'Nehemiah the governor', 1873 (face turned away); Doré's plate (the quiz's own).

could_not_verify: Whether any Greek synaxarion gives Nehemiah a fixed day: not checked; the page says only what the OCA and Azbuka Very show.
The 2004 Roman Martyrology was checked through GCatholic's English rendering, not the Latin book.
Rabbinic traditions (Sanhedrin 93b: Nehemiah identified with Zerubbabel; his book not named for him for speaking ill of his predecessors): only modern copyrighted translations found; left out.
Bede's commentary On Ezra and Nehemiah: no public-domain English translation; left out.
Where he was born and where he is buried: nowhere recorded; left out.

checker_2026_09_25.checked: One light pass. Read the page whole. Checked: the OCA's '445/444 B.C.' and its Sunday of the Forefathers listing; the Heiligen-Lexikon entry (Neemias under 13 July, passed over by the Bollandists because he received no veneration); the 2004 Martyrology's 13 July (Esdras, no Nehemiah) and the 1916 index (Esdras 13 July, no Nehemiah); the ELCA Day of Penitence (Nehemiah 1:4-11a); Ambrose's 'holy Nehemiah' and the baptism reading in Duties book 3; Sulpicius (the passage is in Sacred History 2, chapter 11); Strong's 8660 ('His Excellency'); the ten gates of chapter 3; the four 'Remember me' prayers and the two against his enemies; the BSB wording behind the paraphrased verses, spot-checked. Licences: both Commons files match the page (the Tissot band is from the Internet Archive scan of the 1904 book, public domain).
changed: Nehemiah 3:12: Shallum is 'ruler of the other half-district of Jerusalem' in the BSB, not 'ruler of half of Jerusalem'; the moment now says 'a half-district'.
Capitals for God inside quotations: 'the One Who will grant us success' (2:20) and 'Remember the Lord, Who is great and awesome' (4:14).

The 13 July myth claimed the 1875 dictionary is 'the usual source' of the date, which nothing on disk shows. It now says only what the dictionary does: it lists him under 13 July, but only to say he has no feast. 'There, 13 July is the day of Ezra' became 'In both' (both Martyrologies keep Ezra that day).
left_for_owner: The second picture (the Urbino Bible miniature, 652 px) shows Nehemiah bowed and turned away among a crowd of courtiers: it may fall under his rule 'no figure lost in a crowd scene'. The 1873 gallery engraving shows him kneeling in profile, face turned away. A quick look at Commons' Nehemiah category found nothing better (the colour icon there is modern, the rest are small, black and white, or licensed CC BY-SA). If he dislikes it, the page can go without a portrait (it is optional) and keep the band alone.
checker_2026_09_25.tests: verify-quotes exit 0 (73 quotations, 62 entries); saints-test passed. At a glance unchanged, so no re-measure.
